source_name: ProCredit Bank Kosovo — Lajme / Njoftime (news & customer notices)
why_relevant: ProCredit Kosovo publishes legally required customer notices of changes to general terms and rules; an example notice page ('Ndryshimi i kushteve dhe rregullave te pergjithshme per kliente') was found in search results. Because the bank must give clients ~30 days' notice with an exact effective date, these notices act as a dated mirror of underlying CBK regulation and payment-scheme change.

source_name: ProCredit Bank Kosovo — General Terms and Conditions PDFs (individuals & businesses)
why_relevant: The versioned T&C PDFs carry an explicit 'in force from' date and a version number (e.g. v1.2). Version-to-version diffs expose exactly which clause changed and when, which is the cleanest indirect read-out of a new CBK rule or payment-services requirement in a market with no consolidated public rule tracker.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo — Raporte dhe njoftime (reports & announcements)
why_relevant: RBKO's combined reports-and-announcements hub is the disclosure surface of the largest RBI-owned bank in Kosovo. RBKO's own reporting states it is subject to EU regulatory change through RBI and is therefore pre-adapted to local rules that harmonise with the EU — making its announcements an early indicator of where Kosovo regulation is heading.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo — Lista e tarifave per individe / per biznese (fee schedules)
why_relevant: Fee schedules must be republished with an effective date whenever tariffs change, and tariff changes are frequently regulation-driven (basic payment account caps, payment-services rules, future SEPA pricing). Diffing the tariff list across time is a low-noise proxy for regulatory effective dates and for the cost impact of new rules.

source_name: NLB Banka Kosovo — Cmimorja dhe kushtet e pergjithshme
why_relevant: Single page combining price list and general conditions for the NLB Group subsidiary — the most convenient single URL in the cell for detecting a dated T&C/tariff change. NLB Kosovo also feeds the NLB Group (Ljubljana, listed) disclosure chain, so a local change here is often echoed in group filings.

source_name: NLB Banka Kosovo — IBAN konvertuesi (IBAN converter tool)
why_relevant: A bank-side IBAN conversion utility is the operational fingerprint of the CBK account-numbering regulation (XK05 + 16-digit account = 20 characters). If Kosovo's SEPA accession forces an IBAN/BIC or scheme-message change, this tool and its explanatory copy are among the first customer-facing artefacts to be updated.

source_name: BPB (Banka per Biznes) — Njoftim mbi IBAN
why_relevant: A dedicated standing customer notice explaining the IBAN conversion mandated by the CBK Regulation on the Standard Bank Account Number System, including the XK05 prefix construction. It is a worked example of a bank restating a regulation in customer-facing language with the operative date.

source_name: BPB — 'Hyn ne fuqi rregullorja per qasje ne llogari pagese me sherbime bazike' (basic payment account regulation notice)
why_relevant: The single best proof-of-concept for this cell's thesis: a commercial bank page whose headline literally announces that a CBK regulation on access to basic-services payment accounts has entered into force. The bank page names the regulation and the date, which a public rule tracker in Kosovo does not reliably do.

source_name: BPB — Njoftim per kliente / Lajme (customer notices & news index)
why_relevant: BPB's news/notice index is the container for the regulation-in-force and IBAN notices above and runs in both sq and en, allowing cross-language confirmation of the same regulatory event.

source_name: BPB — Kushtet dhe afatet e pergjithshme per marredhenien bankare
why_relevant: The bank's general banking-relationship terms, including the clause obliging notification of changes at least 30 days before the effective date (shorter where law or regulator requires). That clause itself is the mechanism this whole cell exploits, and its wording changes when the underlying consumer-protection rule changes.

source_name: BKT Kosova — Njoftime (announcements) and 'Njoftim me rendesi per klientet'
why_relevant: BKT Kosova's announcements stream carries pricing-change notices for individuals, services and cards, plus an international-payments notice — the type of item that dates a payments-rule or correspondent/compliance change. BKT is a Turkish-owned (Calik) bank, giving a different regulatory transmission path from the EU-owned peers.

source_name: BKT Kosova — Kushtet e pergjithshme per sherbime bankare individuale (dated PDF versions)
source_subtype: versioned terms document with date-encoded URL
why_relevant: BKT publishes its individual-banking general conditions as serially versioned PDFs under a year/month path (2024/11 -> 2026/03). The document states the one-month advance-notice duty and enumerates the permitted notification channels. The path convention makes version history machine-recoverable, which is rare and valuable.

source_name: TEB Sh.A. Kosovo — Lajme / Njoftim per klientet
why_relevant: TEB (BNP Paribas Fortis / Colakoglu joint venture) publishes customer notices including one stating that the general terms and conditions of the client relationship have changed. As a BNP-affiliated bank it also imports EU-group compliance standards ahead of local rules.

source_name: TEB Sh.A. Kosovo — Cmimorja / Tarifat e pergjithshme (fee schedule PDFs)
why_relevant: TEB names its tariff PDFs with the effective date in the filename (Cmimorja_DD.MM.YYYY.pdf). That convention turns a directory listing into a dated timeline of tariff/regulatory change with zero parsing.

source_name: Banka Ekonomike — Kushtet e pergjithshme te afarizmit te bankes
why_relevant: The only fully domestically-owned systemic bank in the cell — no foreign parent to import EU standards, so its terms track the local CBK rulebook more purely than the subsidiaries do. Useful as a control case to separate genuine Kosovo regulatory change from imported group policy. Banka Ekonomike also received CBK approval to acquire the Turkiye Is Bankasi Kosovo branch, a supervisory event visible via this actor.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Kosova SHA — Per ne / Legal Notice (corporate transformation disclosure)
why_relevant: Ziraat's own pages disclose that from 19 May 2025 the entity converted from a foreign-bank branch (T.C. Ziraat Bankasi A.S. - Dega ne Kosove) into a Kosovo-registered joint-stock company explicitly to comply with local regulatory standards. That is a licensing/supervision change surfaced by the bank rather than by a public regulator feed — exactly the indirect-mirror pattern, and it dates a branch-to-subsidiary supervisory shift affecting foreign-branch banks generally.

source_name: ProCredit Holding — Annual Report & Disclosure Report (Pillar 3), Kosovo segment
why_relevant: ProCredit Holding is Frankfurt-listed and BaFin/ECB-supervised, so its annual and Pillar 3 disclosure reports must describe material regulatory developments in each operating country — including Kosovo — in audited, dated English prose. This is the highest-credibility indirect statement of Kosovo regulatory change available anywhere in this cell.

source_name: ProCredit Bank Kosovo — Annual Reports (local audited accounts)
why_relevant: Local audited annual reports state CBK capital/liquidity requirements actually applied to the bank in the reporting year, and the notes disclose new or amended CBK regulations affecting the accounts. This converts an opaque local rulebook into dated, auditor-checked statements.

source_name: NLB Group (Ljubljana) — Investor relations / financial reports, Kosovo segment
why_relevant: NLB Group reports segment data for Kosovo alongside Serbia and Montenegro and discloses regulatory approvals for its regional transactions. Quarterly cadence makes it a faster regulatory read-out than annual reports, and it triangulates the Kosovo picture from a Slovenian-listed, ECB-supervised issuer.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG — Annual Reports (Kosovo network unit)
why_relevant: RBI's group reporting covers Kosovo as a network unit and frames Kosovo's rulemaking as harmonising toward EU regulation — the explicit transmission mechanism this cell is built on. Group-level risk and regulatory sections often flag a coming Kosovo requirement before it appears locally.

source_name: Kosovo Banking Association (Shoqata e Bankave te Kosoves) — Compliance and AML professional committees
why_relevant: The association's committee pages name the sitting Heads of Compliance and Heads of AML at the member banks (e.g. ProCredit and NLB chairs/vice-chairs). That is a ready-made actor map for the compliance function across the whole cell, and the committees are the forum where CBK draft regulations are collectively commented on — a pointer into the consultation channel.

source_name: CBK list of licensed/registered financial institutions (bank-perimeter reference)
why_relevant: Not a bank site, but the authoritative dated roster that defines which private banks exist to be monitored in this cell. Needed to keep the crawl perimeter correct as entities enter, convert (Ziraat branch to SHA) or are absorbed (Turkiye Is Bankasi branch into Banka Ekonomike). Dated file path gives a versioned membership timeline.

source_name: ProCredit Bank Kosovo — Serbian-language e-banking manuals and customer documentation
why_relevant: The only concrete Serbian-language customer documentation found on a Kosovo bank domain in this pass. Operational manuals restate limits, notification (obavestenje) behaviour and payment mechanics, so they change when payment rules change — and they establish that ProCredit maintains an .sr documentation track worth watching for Serbian-language notices.

source_name: Fibank Kosova — Kushtet e punes (terms in force from a stated date)
why_relevant: A smaller Kosovo bank (Bulgarian First Investment Bank group) that encodes the effective date directly in the filename ('ne fuqi nga 21 Shkurt 2026'). Smaller banks change terms in lockstep with the sector when a rule bites, so they serve as corroboration that a change is regulation-driven rather than a single bank's commercial decision.

source_name: BQK — Lajme & Ngjarje (News and Events feed, Central Bank of Kosovo)
why_relevant: Primary announcement channel where BQK publishes conferences, workshops, MoUs, donor-project launches and closing events. Weak signals about rules under preparation (e.g. crypto-asset/digital-money policy frameworks, payment services law) surface here as event news weeks or months before any draft regulation appears in the legal section.

source_name: BQK — dedicated conference agenda pages (e.g. 25th anniversary conference agenda)
why_relevant: BQK publishes standalone agenda pages for its own conferences. Agendas name the officials, the sessions and the policy themes under preparation — exactly the pre-legislative artefact this cell targets.

source_name: BQK Regional Conference on Crypto-assets and Digital Money (with IMF) — Prishtina
why_relevant: Concrete instance of the weak-signal pattern: a BQK+IMF conference themed 'policy and regulatory frameworks in a changing environment', with IMF's Tobias Adrian and regional governors, held 3-4 June in Prishtina. Signals a crypto-asset/digital-money regulatory workstream ahead of any published rule. Media coverage supplies agenda detail and named participants.
